papers.title: Asymmetric Delay-Induced Translation in Displacement Formations
papers.abstract: This letter studies a structural consequence of reciprocal delay asymmetry in first-order displacement-based formation control. Under an admissible delay margin, the prescribed displacement formation is preserved, while unequal reciprocal measurement delays destroy the nominal gradient structure of the closed-loop dynamics and activate the translational nullspace. As a result, the formation exhibits persistent rigid-body translation generated purely by endogenous interactions, without any external input or reference. We establish an explicit link between internal-force cancellation, centroid dynamics, and delay-induced discrepancy signals, and show that the locked collective velocity is determined by the transient accumulation of reciprocal delay asymmetry through the auxiliary layer. The admissible delay size is defined through the characteristic roots of the projected retarded system, so the locking mechanism is supported by a shape-convergence and discrepancy-integrability guarantee in this delay-margin regime. The synchronized reciprocal-delay case and the zero/nonzero velocity cases are also characterized. Simulations on a baseline triangular formation, a larger sparse connected graph, and single-edge delay-asymmetry sweeps support the analysis and show that the locked translation is quantitatively modulated by the reciprocal delay pattern.

papers.title: Improved IQC Covers for Sample-and-Hold
papers.abstract: Two methods are presented to advance the modular paradigm of covering the periodic and synchronous sample-and-hold operator with a nominal model plus IQC-bounded error. First, we observe that error IQCs satisfied by one model induce error IQCs satisfied by other models. Second, new IQCs are obtained by Fourier analysis and treatment of the error path as an operator whose gain can be tractably bounded. These tools are used to obtain new static and dynamic error IQCs, including IQCs for a new rational model. Improvement is demonstrated on examples including$\mathcal {L}_{2}$performance analysis of a structured uncertain sampled-data Lur’e system.

papers.title: The Geometry of Coordinated Trajectories for Non-Stop Flying Carriers Holding a Cable-Suspended Load
papers.abstract: This work considers the problem of using multiple aerial carriers to hold a cable-suspended load while remaining in periodic motion at all times. Using a novel differential geometric perspective, it is shown that the problem may be recast as that of finding an immersion of the unit circle into the smooth manifold of admissible configurations. Additionally, this manifold is shown to be path connected under a mild assumption on the attachment points of the carriers to the load. Based on these ideas, a family of simple linear solutions to the original problems is presented that overcomes the constraints of alternative solutions previously proposed in the literature. Simulation results demonstrate the flexibility of the theory in identifying suitable solutions.

papers.title: A Class of Generalized Sufficiently Smooth Projection Operators
papers.abstract: We propose novel sufficiently smooth projection operators for adaptive control of a class of continuous-time nonlinear systems subject to uncertain parameters. We show: 1) stability of the set where both the plant state is in the target set and the estimate equals the uncertain parameter; 2) robust and uniform global asymptotic stability of the set above, whenever a solution-independent rank condition is satisfied on the target set; and 3) each bounded plant state approaches the target set. Compared with the existing strategies, we show that the proposed projection operators can be designed to increase computational efficiency, fasten adaptation for large estimation errors, or smooth control. We provide numerical simulations to illustrate the effectiveness and versatility of the proposed controller.

papers.title: Inverse variational Kalman filter for adversarial sensing
papers.abstract: Adversarial sensing is a security related problem in cyber physical systems (CPS), where a defender controlled target may be tracked by a non-cooperative adversary. The inverse filters, which are launched on the defender, have emerged as tools to infer the exposure of defender’s state to the adversary, which employs a standard filter (referred to as forward filter in this letter), such as Kalman filter, to recursively estimate the defender’s state. This letter proposes an inverse variational Kalman filter (IVKF), which extends the inverse Kalman filter to unknown and even time-varying adversarial measurement noise covariance (MNC) that plays an essential role in the forward (i.e., standard) filtering algorithms. The idea is to jointly estimate the inverse state and adversarial MNC, while the MNC cannot be straightforwardly estimated. Thus, the variational Bayesian (VB) framework is leveraged, and the stochastic natural gradient VB (SNGVB) inference is derived so as to solve the problem of non-conjugacy in computing the posterior of MNC. The performance of proposed IVKF is validated through simulations.

papers.title: Reference Condensation for Model Predictive Control With Preview
papers.abstract: In model predictive control (MPC), preview information can greatly improve tracking. Including preview information does, however, increase the parameter dimension linearly with the preview horizon, which increases online cost and, more importantly, the complexity of explicit MPC. We introduce reference condensation, a method that compresses a future reference trajectory into a single setpoint through a linear map. For the unconstrained tracking problem, the map follows from a least-squares projection. For receding-horizon MPC, we also study a weighted variant that prioritizes the first applied control. Numerical experiments on a double integrator and a higher-order aircraft example show that the weighted condensation closely matches full preview while keeping the parameter dimension independent of the preview horizon.

papers.title: Temporal Segmentation Endows Networks With Strong Structural Controllability
papers.abstract: Restoring the controllability of networked systems under structural constraints is an important control problem. However, establishing controllability without altering the network structure or introducing additional external controllers remains an open challenge. A temporal segmentation strategy is developed to transform a static network that is not strongly structurally controllable into a temporal network. By utilizing the characteristics of temporal network, strong structural controllability can be restored while preserving the original network edges and external controller configuration. Specifically, the proposed segmentation scheme constructs each snapshot as a serial buds cactus structure, thereby guaranteeing strong structural controllability of the resulting temporal network, independent of the snapshot durations. Based on this structural characterization, an efficient segmentation algorithm is further developed to construct the required snapshots. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Energy-Aware Consensus Control for Multi-Agent Systems With Guaranteed Battery Safety via H-Infinity LMI Design
papers.abstract: In this letter, we propose an energy-aware consensus control framework for multi-agent systems (MASs) with guaranteed battery safety through linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Since battery-powered agents such as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have limited energy, conventional consensus strategies may induce aggressive control inputs, risking over-discharging and operational failures. To address this issue, we introduce state-of-charge (SOC)-dependent interaction weights that reduce the control burden on energy-depleted agents, resulting in a SOC-dependent Laplacian matrix. An observer-based control framework is then developed, where the observer and controller gains are synthesized using$H_{\infty } $and polytopic LMI formulations, respectively. Based on these gains, sufficient conditions for battery safety are established, providing a computable safe operation horizon. The proposed framework is validated via a MAS formation control example.

papers.title: A Koopman Set-Membership Approach for Nonlinear Data-Driven Control With Stability Guarantees
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a data-driven controller design method for unknown nonlinear systems based on a Koopman bilinear realization. Using Koopman operator theory, the nonlinear system can be represented as a bilinear discrete-time system with a residual error term. The residual error is proportionally bounded by the norm of the lifted state and input, while the system matrices of the bilinear model are unknown. Assuming that bounds on the residual error are available, the unknown system matrices are characterized via a set-membership representation using the collected input-state data pairs of the nonlinear system. A data-driven controller design method is proposed to ensure stability for all bilinear systems within this set-membership description and for all admissible residual errors. More specifically, we design a rational state-feedback controller that stabilizes the bilinear model with residual error and, consequently, the original nonlinear system, by solving a sum-of-squares (SOS) program. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is demonstrated through numerical examples.

papers.title: Privacy-Convergence Rate Co-Design for Exact Average Consensus
papers.abstract: We study the joint design of privacy and convergence rate for deterministic exact average consensus on strongly connected directed networks. Privacy is observability-based: an honest-but-curious agent must not recover another agent’s datum from its local trajectory. Using exact privacy distance as the deterministic metric, we pose two dual weight-design problems: fastest consensus under a privacy floor, and most private consensus under a convergence-rate ceiling. We prove finite-horizon stabilization of the metric and existence of solutions on compact rank-regular admissible subsets. A row-softmax parameterization enables offline weight design, while a reproducible grid yields empirically nondominated curves on odd cycles and an irregular eight-agent graph, with 6.0–10.5% faster convergence at a fixed exact margin and a 13.5–33.0% larger encoding amplitude at fixed rate, raising the statistical estimation-error floor under noise, while the noiseless normalized margin is a design-invariant graph constant. We further prove an exact-to-statistical lower bound and a formal separation from finite ε-DP, showing that non-recoverability and noise-based indistinguishability address complementary threat models.

papers.title: Variational Control Principle Based on Free Energy Minimization
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a variational control principle grounded in the minimization of free energy on Riemannian manifolds. Unlike classical approaches that treat stability, constraints, and adaptation as separate problems, the proposed framework integrates them into a single variational principle. Control laws, including adaptive parameter updates, are derived as natural gradient flows. This geometric structure inherently enforces hard constraints via barrier potentials, eliminating the need for discontinuous projection operators, while an entropy term provides regularization and robustness. Rigorous analysis establishes the passivity and input-to-state stability of the resulting closed-loop systems. The proposed framework seamlessly bridges the gap between adaptive control and direct state-feedback design. Numerical examples illustrate the method’s geometric anti-windup properties, robustness to disturbances, and the explicit role of entropic smoothing in improving numerical conditioning.

papers.title: Eigenstructure Assignment of Output-Nulling Friends by Sylvester Mapping
papers.abstract: This letter studies eigenstructure assignment of output-nulling friends for linear time-invariant systems. The internal and external assignment equations are reformulated as generalized Sylvester equations associated with the Rosenbrock polynomial matrix and the state-input polynomial matrix. The prescribed target matrices need not be in Jordan form. This permits the direct use of companion or block-companion, real Schur, or other convenient target coordinates. A complete parameterization is established based on the Sylvester mapping and the Smith form, separating all solutions into a polynomial right-nullspace part and a local torsion part. The latter is crucial for eigenstructure assignment at invariant zeros and for defective invariant-zero chains. Within the split-realization class, the framework parameterizes all output-nulling friends admitting a closed-loop invariant complement that carries the prescribed external structure. Fixed left-kernel bases convert the torsion constraints into unconstrained Smith-coordinate parameters. The contribution is exact, structural, and target-coordinate-covariant. When the target spectrum avoids the relevant rank-drop set, state-direction-space dimension formulas are extended to arbitrary target matrices.

papers.title: Bipartite Tracking Consensus in Signed Graph Games: A Data-Driven Inverse RL Approach
papers.abstract: This letter investigates inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) for leader-follower multi-agent systems (LFMASs) over signed graphs, a scenario where existing graphical game frameworks fail due to their assumption of non-negative edge weights. We consider a practical setting where a learner LFMAS imitates the optimal behavior of an expert LFMAS without knowing the expert’s cost functions. A graphical apprentice game is formulated on signed graphs, and a distributed data-driven IRL algorithm is proposed, enabling the learner to recover equivalent reward weights and replicate the expert’s policies. Theoretical analysis guarantees convergence to the expert’s reward structure and closed-loop stability of the learner system. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Reachability-Envelope-Constrained Operational-Space Control for Soft Continuum Arms
papers.abstract: Reachability limits in soft continuum arms are commonly handled outside the feedback loop through workspace estimation, reference selection, or constrained optimization. This letter develops a reachability-envelope-constrained operational-space controller that incorporates a precomputed ellipsoidal outer envelope into the feedback design. Under a piecewise constant curvature representation, curvature, segment-length, and Jacobian-regularity limits define a compact regular deformation set. Retained samples from its task-space image are enclosed by the ellipsoid, while continuous-set inclusion requires a certified enclosing bound. A closed-form reference-conditioning map creates an explicit tracking margin, and an ellipsoidal barrier Lyapunov function guarantees forward invariance of the admissible error set and asymptotic tracking on the regular operating set. The method avoids online optimization and repeated feasibility projection. Configuration-dependent simulations show envelope-consistent tracking; the simulated curvature, segment-length, and Jacobian-regularity measures remain within their prescribed limits.

papers.title: Dynamic State-Feedback Synthesis for Positive Systems With Nonnegative Inputs
papers.abstract: This letter develops a dynamic state-feedback synthesis framework with positive controller dynamics for linear positive systems subject to nonnegative input constraints. The proposed framework ensures nonnegative control inputs through positive controller dynamics, avoiding explicit nonnegative constraints on static feedback gains. By incorporating the controller dynamics into the closed-loop system, an augmented positive-system formulation is established, yielding necessary and sufficient conditions for positivity and asymptotic stability, which are further transformed into an equivalent linear programming formulation for controller synthesis. The relationship between dynamic and static state-feedback designs is established, showing that the proposed dynamic realization recovers the static feasible gain set and has a supremal Lyapunov-certified decay rate no smaller than that of the corresponding static controller. Numerical examples demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Internal Dissipation Allocation in Control Lyapunov Function Design
papers.abstract: This letter studies how control Lyapunov function (CLF) structure affects CLF-based control under input constraints. In relaxed CLF-based quadratic programs (CLF–QPs), a mismatch between the prescribed dissipation and the CLF-induced input channel may cause excessive actuation demand, increased relaxation, and chattering-like behavior near the zero-channel set. A recursive backstepping representation exposes the internal dissipation and shows that uniformly increasing recursive dissipation strengthens zero-channel dissipation but also raises downstream actuation demand. To reshape this trade-off, a Lyapunov-level allocation mechanism redesigns the virtual controls, recursive coordinates, and dissipation profile. Simulations on a nonlinear spring–damper system illustrate the weak-channel effect and the dissipation–actuation trade-off, and show that the shaped CLF achieves convergence and disturbance attenuation comparable to high-gain uniform designs with lower control effort and a substantially smaller relaxation level.

papers.title: PID-Compatible Compensation for Containerized Wireless Industrial Control Under Timing Uncertainty
papers.abstract: Timing uncertainty in containerized wireless industrial control arises from the combined effects of wireless communication, protocol processing, and container virtualization. This letter proposes a reinforcement learning (RL)-assisted proportional–integral–derivative (PID)-compatible compensation framework for such uncertainty. A nonlinear controller-level model represents bounded delay and correlated read/write losses while distinguishing candidate from plant-applied inputs. A closed-form, safety-projected additive compensator retains the PID structure, while a cloud-trained RL policy schedules the controller parameters. Sufficient conditions are derived for uniform ultimate boundedness of the tracking error on a compact validation region under intermittent communication failures. Quadruple-tank results show that the proposed method achieves the lowest mean squared error, integral absolute error, and worst-case settling time among all evaluated methods, including fixed and robust controllers.

papers.title: Safe Output Tracking of Boolean Control Networks via Feasible-Domain Analysis
papers.abstract: This letter studies safe output tracking of Boolean control networks with respect to a Boolean reference system. The objective is to construct a feedback matrix such that the system avoids forbidden states and achieves finite-time safe output tracking from admissible initial conditions. By deleting forbidden states and forming a reduced augmented system with the reference system, the problem is converted into a feasible-domain characterization problem. A matrix criterion is established for global safe output tracking. When the criterion is not satisfied, the same fixed-point computation yields the maximal feasible domain and a feedback matrix on this domain. An algorithm is provided for the domain computation and feedback design, and examples illustrate both non-global and global safe tracking cases.

papers.title: Nonlinear-Gain Distributed Zeroth-Order Optimization for Networked Black-Box Control
papers.abstract: This letter studies distributed stochastic optimization over a peer-to-peer network when agents can query only zeroth-order function values. We propose ZOOM-PB, a coordinate-sampling method that blends each local ZO estimate with a fractional-power response while maintaining only a primal state. The raw estimate is retained as a linear anchor, and the nonlinear mixing weight is coupled to the optimization stepsize. This design is motivated by a basic obstruction: transforming heterogeneous or noisy local estimates before averaging can reverse the network direction. We bound that nonlinear residual directly from the raw oracle assumptions instead of imposing an aggregate-alignment condition. With a smooth stochastic-function oracle and a connected graph, ZOOM-PB attains the nonconvex stationarity order $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{p/(nT)})$ and a Polyak--Łojasiewicz statistical term of order $\mathcal{O}(p/(nT))$, after an explicit initialization transient. Numerical examples compare ZOOM-PB with seven distributed ZO baselines under matched query and message budgets.

papers.title: Agent Utilities Over Generalized Voronoi Regions and Their Gradients
papers.abstract: In this paper, we generalize the concept of Voronoi regions, define agent utility as the integral of a utility density over the corresponding Voronoi region, derive gradients of the utility, and illustrate the approach in a two-team example from soccer. The generalization of Voronoi regions is in the form of so-called Cost-Induced Voronoi (CIV) regions, where the agent state space may differ from the space being partitioned. One example of such regions is when the cost is given by the optimal solution of an LQR control problem. Then the agent states include position as well as velocity, while the partitioned space only includes positions. The agent utility is defined by integrating some utility density over the CIV region of the agent. This utility density might be the probability density of some beneficial event, such as receiving a pass in soccer. The utility is then the overall probability of receiving a pass and the gradient represents a way to improve that probability. We show how this utility gradient can be computed using the Reynolds Transport Theorem from fluid mechanics, and that this approach achieves similar accuracy while reducing computation time by about an order of magnitude compared to a baseline finite-difference approximation.

papers.title: Bilinear Input Modulation for Mamba: A State-Input Product Prior for Memory Retention and Multiplicative Computation
papers.abstract: Selective State Space Models (SSMs), notably Mamba, employ diagonal state transitions that limit both memory retention and bilinear computational capacity. We propose a factorized bilinear input modulation that augments the SSM with a state-input product. The bilinear form arising in Koopman control theory serves as a structural prior that identifies this missing term. After introducing a shared state across channels (Coupled SSM), the bilinear modulation admits two placements. Coupled Bilinear Input Modulation (seq-BIM) places the full bilinear product on the input side at the cost of sequential computation, and Parallel Bilinear Input Modulation (p-BIM) places the same bilinear product on the state transition while remaining parallel-scannable. Experiments on a multiple input-delay pendulum (memory retention) and NARMA-10 (bilinear computation) show that both bilinear variants improve memory retention and bilinear computation simultaneously over Standard and Coupled baselines. A pathway ablation shows that the bilinear signal acts mainly through the selectivity pathway for seq-BIM. The improvement is statistically robust, with the bilinear variants consistently outperforming the other variants on bilinear computation. Furthermore, only the bilinear variants benefit from increasing the SSM state dimension, while coupling alone shows no improvement, establishing the bilinear mechanism as uniquely capable of exploiting larger state spaces.

papers.title: Finite-Time Bipartite Consensus for Multi-Agent Systems With Hidden Markov Switching Topologies
papers.abstract: This letter addresses the problem of finite-time bipartite consensus in probability for multi-agent systems (MASs) subject to hidden Markov switching topologies. Since it is impractical to obtain accurate mode information of switching topologies, the hidden Markov model (HMM) is adopted to deal with this issue. Asynchronous controllers, whose modes are determined by conditional probabilities, are designed to operate without requiring perfect synchronization with the topological switches. An extended switching matrix$W_{\alpha } $representing cooperative-competitive interactions is employed, which avoids the need for gauge transformation. Within this unified framework, by constructing a mode-dependent quadratic Lyapunov function, sufficient conditions are derived for achieving finite-time bipartite consensus/stability in probability under structurally balanced/unbalanced topologies. Simulation results demonstrate the validity of the proposed approach.

papers.abstract: We present a new algorithm for the design of maximum hands-off hybrid control sequences for discrete-time switched linear systems that satisfy pre-specified restrictions on the admissible actions and steer a given initial state of the switched system to the origin of the state-space in a pre-specified duration of time. The key apparatuses for our analysis are state-space abstraction and graph theory. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate our results.

papers.title: Amplitude-Dependent Bode Diagrams via Scaled Relative Graphs
papers.abstract: Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) provide an intuitive graphical frequency-domain method for the analysis of Nonlinear (NL) systems, generalizing the Nyquist diagram. In this paper, we develop a method for computing $L_2$-gain bounds for Lur'e systems over bounded frequency and amplitude ranges. We do this by restricting the input space of the SRG both in frequency and energy content, and using methods from Sobolev theory. The resulting gain bounds over restricted sets of inputs are less conservative than bounds computed over the entire $L_2$, and yield three-dimensional NL generalization of the Bode diagram, plotting $L_2$-gain as function of both input frequency and energy content. In the zero-energy limit, the Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) Bode diagram is recovered, and at the infinite-energy zero-frequency limit, we recover the $L_2$-gain. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated on an example that resembles Phase-Locked Loop dynamics.

papers.title: Quantization and Sampled Implementation of the Super-Twisting Sliding Mode Control
papers.abstract: Solving control problems under finite-valued actuation is challenging because the input can only be selected from a prescribed admissible set, rather than adjusted continuously. This difficulty is amplified when the input is updated at fixed sampling instants in a sample-and-hold fashion. This letter studies these constraints for the super-twisting sliding mode algorithm (STA). In the letter it is shown that the quantisation error enters through the same channel as the disturbance. Consequently, by incorporating the quantisation bound into the gain selection, the finite-valued STA can still enforce finite-time convergence. The analysis is then extended to sampled implementation. This yields practical finite-time convergence to a compact neighbourhood of the sliding manifold, whose size increases with the update period. Numerical examples illustrate the validity of the key-findings of this letter.

papers.title: A Novel Criterion on Almost Sure Safety and Stochastic Safety-Critical Control With Joint Performance
papers.abstract: Stochastic disturbances could hinder safety guarantee which, however, is indispensable for engineering systems. Some effort has gone into safety-critical control of stochastic systems, particularly with the aid of stochastic zeroing control barrier functions (ZCBFs). This letter seeks to ease off stochastic ZCBF conditions of safety verification, so as to circumvent performance/constraint confliction in safety-critical control. Specifically, a novel criterion on almost sure safety is established, with the stochastic ZCBF condition obeyed only in a neighbourhood of the boundary of safe set. The verification scope of ZCBF condition is substantially reduced, in contrast to the related results where the stochastic ZCBF conditions need verifying in the entire safe set. Based on the criterion, safety-critical control with joint performance is addressed for stochastic nonlinear systems. Two or multiple controller candidates are united by a convex combination with state-dependent weights, ensuring the stochastic ZCBF condition around the boundary of safe set and other performance-guarantee condition in a certain safe subset. This enables asymptotic stabilization with almost sure safety and multi-constraint stochastic safety-critical control.

papers.title: Controllability of Isothermal Autocatalytic Chemical Reaction
papers.abstract: In this letter, we study the approximate controllability of a semilinear reaction-diffusion system arising from an isothermal autocatalytic chemical reaction. The system is considered on a bounded smooth domain subject to homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and is formulated as an abstract Cauchy problem on the product space$\text {L}^{{2}}\text {(}\Omega \text {)}\times \text {L}^{{2}}\text {(}\Omega \text {)}$. The nonlinear source term consists of positive power functions and is shown to satisfy a Hölder-type continuity condition under the suitable parameter restriction. Using the approximate controllability of the associated linear control system, a Gramian-based control construction, and the Leray-Schauder fixed point theorem, we prove the existence of mild solutions corresponding to regularized controls. Consequently, the semilinear reaction-diffusion system is shown to be approximately controllable on a finite time interval.

papers.title: Deployment-Aware Controller and Control Architecture Co-Design via Mixed-Integer Output-Feedback SLS
papers.abstract: We study controller and control-architecture co-design for output-feedback systems under a hard budget. The architecture activates sensors and actuators and selects among directed communication-service options with specified delivery bounds and costs. Direct optimization over controller transfer matrices and discrete deployments is mixed-integer nonconvex; convex alternatives fix the architecture, use regularization, or impose a quadratically invariant (QI) controller-information pattern. We instead optimize finite impulse response (FIR) output-feedback system-level synthesis (OF-SLS) responses. Binary variables select devices and service options; cumulative binaries record whether the selected service can deliver by each FIR lag. Indicator constraints zero response coefficients that would require unavailable messages. For fixed device and OF-SLS realization-state locations, this yields an exact mixed-integer convex program (MICP) over finite service menus and deployment constraints. Every feasible response admits the standard OF-SLS implementation using only the selected devices and services. In a three-follower platoon, 2736 of 139,968 stabilizable and detectable deployments are QI-compatible. All three actuators are necessary, whereas intermediate-budget optima retain strict subsets of seven sensor packages. At a common budget, the best QI design has 3.86 times the performance loss of the co-design optimum relative to the dense deployment.

papers.title: Multi-Robot Bearing-Based Pose Estimation via Angle Rigidity
papers.abstract: This letter proposes a novel distributed pose estimator for multi-robot systems evolving on$\text {SE}(3)$. The robots’ positions are estimated in$\mathbb {R}^{3}$using angles computed from body-frame bearings, without requiring orientation knowledge. The robots’ orientations are then recovered in$\text {SO(3)}$from the estimated positions, together with bearing and bearing-rate measurements. The estimator accommodates directed sensing topologies and requires only infinitesimal angle rigidity (IAR), which relaxes the requirement, common in bearing-only approaches, that every robot acquire at least two bearings. Unlike existing angle-only schemes, the proposed method also estimates the robots’ orientations. We prove local uniform exponential stability of the observer, assuming that a subset of robots executes persistently exciting motions. These theoretical results are corroborated through numerical simulations.

papers.title: Event-Triggered Adaptive Backstepping–Geometric Control for Nano-Quadrotors
papers.abstract: This letter presents an event-triggered adaptive geometric tracking controller for a nano-quadrotor with uncertain mass and inertia. The research contributions are threefold. First, concurrent mass and inertia adaptation is unified under a single composite Lyapunov function on${\text {SO}}\text {(3)}$in which the translational–rotational coupling is bounded explicitly. The translational loop is input-to-state stable with respect to a bounded rotational residual, and the interconnection is certified as a cascade rather than as two separate subsystems. Second, continuous adaptation is achieved through an event trigger. The held estimate is updated only when the respective measurement-error term could violate the Lyapunov decrease condition and the tracking error lies outside its dead-zone ball. This handles abrupt payload changes and slow battery-induced drift without a separate detector, and rejects noise between events. Third, the two asynchronous triggers acting on the same coupled trajectory are shown to be jointly non-Zeno with index-independent minimum inter-event times, while the control input is computed at every sample. The controller achieves sub-millimeter hover regulation and a${2.3}$cm figure-eight tracking error under a 55% payload, matching the continuously-adapting baseline while reducing parameter updates by 96– 97%.

papers.title: Explicit Ensemble Mean Synchronization for Time Scale Generation With Mixed Atomic Clock Ensembles
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a mixed ensemble containing a mixture of cesium-type and hydrogen maser-type atomic clocks. For the mixed ensemble, the conventional Kalman filtering algorithm has certain limitations due to divergence of the error covariance matrix. To overcome these limitations, we obtain a Kalman filtering algorithm based on observable canonical decomposition that does not have any diverging terms. We use the estimates from the transformed Kalman filter to propose a time scale generation algorithm called explicit ensemble mean synchronization algorithm for the mixed ensemble. In this algorithm, we synchronize the time deviation of each clock from the ideal clock behavior to the unobservable ensemble mean of the phases where the weighting can be decided by the user. By regulating the free-running dynamics associated with the unobservable state, through choosing an appropriate weight vector, the frequency stability of the generated time scale or the synchronized time shared by the clocks is optimized over shorter (resp. longer) intervals, as measured by Hadamard variance. An illustrative example is given to demonstrate the efficiency of our algorithm.

papers.title: Stability of Stochastic Switched Time-Delay Systems With Unstable Subsystems via Piecewise Lyapunov–Krasovskii Functionals
papers.abstract: In view of the issue of excessive conservatism in traditional time-delay handling methods for the$p$th-moment exponential stability analysis of complex stochastic dynamic systems jointly affected by Markov switching and time-delay, this letter proposes a time-delay segmentation method: the global variation interval of the time-delay is divided into continuous subintervals, and the stability analysis conditions corresponding to the subintervals are dynamically matched based on the real-time value of the time-delay. We first focuses on nonlinear switched stochastic time-delay systems, overcomes the limitation that conventional methods solely rely on the global bounds of time-delay, and constructs a piecewise Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional that is doubly dependent on both the time-delay subinterval and the system mode. Furthermore, for the Markov switching stochastic neural network systems with unstable subsystems, a multiple Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional is constructed to tackle the coupling issue between the segmented time-delay and subsystem instability, and the corresponding stability is deduced. Finally, a numerical example verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: LoRA-RC: Reservoir Computing with Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.abstract: Reservoir computing (RC) trains only a linear readout over a fixed recurrent layer, making it fast and data-efficient for online prediction. However, a static reservoir degrades under system drift, readout-only adaptation is then insufficient, and unconstrained reservoir adaptation can destroy the echo-state and incremental stability properties that make RC reliable. This paper proposes LoRA-RC, which adapts the recurrent matrix through a low-rank correction driven by streaming prediction errors. The base reservoir and adaptation bases are fixed offline; a small core matrix is adapted online, projected onto a spectral-norm ball, and low-pass filtered at each step. The projection guarantees that every applied recurrent matrix remains within a certified contraction set, and an incremental input-to-state stability bound is established for the reservoir along each online adaptation path, with path-independent rate and gain. On a Lorenz system with an abrupt parameter drift, LoRA-RC cuts post-drift prediction error by 56% versus a fixed RC and 51% versus readout-only adaptation; ablations over 20 seeds show that removing the projection inflates this error by more than a factor of 40.

papers.title: Detection–Control Games under Hidden Modes: Resilience-Induced Blindness Phenomenon
papers.abstract: This paper studies resilient control for cyber-physical systems operating under hidden degraded or compromised modes. We formulate hidden-mode detection and belief-dependent control as a game between two decision makers with different objectives: the detector seeks informative belief updates, while the controller seeks regulation performance. This objective mismatch shows why the usual separation intuition between detector design and controller design may fail, leading to a performance-reversal phenomenon induced by the resilience of the controller. For a two-mode linear Gaussian system, we theoretically characterize this phenomenon by linking the resilience margin to the log-likelihood evidence. The analysis shows that a well-performing controller with a large resilience margin can suppress mode-dependent information and slow belief adaptation, which in turn degrades the control performance. The resilience-induced blindness phenomenon and its partial mitigation through increased detector sensitivity are illustrated in numerical simulations.

papers.title: Control-Aware Random Access as a Mean-Field Game With a Pigouvian Fix
papers.abstract: We study massive wireless networked control as a stationary Mean-Field Game (MFG) of control-aware random access. Each unstable plant incurs a control-derived covariance cost that grows exponentially with the time since its last successful packet. The covariance follows a piecewise-deterministic Markov process, while the delivery probability decreases with the aggregate offered load. We derive a bang-bang threshold best response and reduce the equilibrium exactly to one scalar load equation. An equilibrium exists under a uniform stability condition and is unique under an explicit contraction. For exponential congestion, we prove selfish over-transmission under$\beta \eta \bar {\lambda } \lt 4$. We then construct a marginal-congestion price that makes a social optimum a taxed equilibrium. It implements that optimum uniquely when the taxed equilibrium is unique. Numerical results validate the scalar reduction and quantify the welfare correction.

papers.title: Adaptive Output Feedback Control for a Class of Uncertain Nonlinear Systems With Performance Constraint via a Quantized Event-Triggered Control Scheme
papers.abstract: In this letter, an adaptive quantized event-triggered output feedback backstepping strategy for uncertain nonlinear systems via preassigned prescribed performance is depicted. To cope with immeasurable states, a feasible filter containing the quantized signal is presented. By applying the intituled preassigned finite-time performance function (PFTPF) and adaptive quantized event-triggered backstepping algorithm, the developed control algorithm guarantees that not only all the signals of the closed-loop system are bounded, but also the restricted tracking error variable tends to a specified zone in finite time. Ultimately, the availability of our designed quantized event-triggered control method was addressed by giving simulation results.

papers.title: Beware of Temporal Correlation of the Uncertainty in Stochastic Predictive Control
papers.abstract: In robust predictive control, temporal correlations of the uncertainty are often neglected without compromising constraint satisfaction, since robust guarantees depend only on the uncertainty support. This intuition no longer applies to stochastic predictive control with chance constraints: even for identical marginal distributions, different temporal dependence structures can yield different violation probabilities.In this letter, the influence of the temporal correlation of the uncertainties in stochastic predictive control is analyzed from the perspective of distributional ambiguity. We turn to the Bures-Wasserstein distance and state the distance between the uncorrelated and the fully positively correlated case for arbitrary distributions based on the joint covariance structure. Furthermore, we show that the ambiguity ball centered at the uncorrelated distribution and just including the fully correlated distribution includes all admissible covariance structures consistent with the marginal distribution. We present a formulation of linear chance constraints which is distributionally robust against ambiguity in the temporal correlation and show how the Bures-Wasserstein distance can be used to further restrict the ambiguity set.

papers.title: Finite-Time Consensus With Unknown Constant Delays via a Graph-Embedded Emulator
papers.abstract: This letter establishes exact finite-time average consensus for driftless agents with unknown, possibly heterogeneous constant actuation delays and a known common upper bound. A command emulator, initialized once from the physical state and driven by the undelayed command, reproduces the physical trajectories without delay knowledge. Since the plant is not measured thereafter, the scheme is an open-loop command generator with nominal exactness. Under zero-command initialization, a graph-embedded Lyapunov–Krasovskii functional, equivalently represented by the emulator, yields an exact Dini dissipation identity and delay-independent finite-time certificate. We establish the admissible edge-potential family, tightness condition, uncleared-buffer bias, extension to fully actuated driftless systems, exact quadratic command effort, and terminal-disagreement bounds under disturbances, delay mismatch, and initialization error. A mobile-cart study validates the delay-independent transient and predicted degradation.

papers.title: Online Optimization With Unknown Time-Varying Parameters Using Noisy Gradient Measurements
papers.abstract: We study online optimization problems in which the cost function depends on latent, time-varying parameters that are unmeasurable and governed by unknown dynamics. Specifically, we consider a strongly convex cost function whose linear term evolves according to unknown linear stochastic dynamics about an unknown nominal operating point, while the algorithm has access only to finite noisy gradient measurements. We propose a solution that uses control theoretic tools to reconstruct the latent parameters from gradient observations using a Gauss-Markov estimator, then identifies the parameter dynamics using a bias-reduced instrumental variable estimator, and finally forecasts the parameters to compute the minimizer. We provide a high probability, finite-horizon bound on the expected tracking error. We illustrate our algorithm on a series of numerical examples.

papers.title: Online LQG Control of Stochastic Systems With Unknown Noise Covariances via Covariance-Equivalent ARMAX Identification
papers.abstract: This letter addresses online Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG) control for stochastic systems with unknown process and measurement noise covariances. Although conventional adaptive Kalman filtering methods estimate these covariances from innovation data, identifiability limitations, particularly for the process noise covariance, can lead to inaccurate filter gains and degraded closed-loop performance. To avoid explicit covariance estimation, this letter proposes an online covariance-equivalent LQG (OCE-LQG) method. The Kalman prior-estimation dynamics are reformulated as an ARMAX innovation model, where the covariance-dependent information is captured by the moving-average (MA) coefficients. These coefficients are recursively estimated using an extended least-squares algorithm under a strictly positive-real condition and then used to construct an equivalent LQG controller. The proposed controller is shown to converge to the covariance-known LQG controller in the Cesàro sense and achieve the same infinite-horizon average quadratic cost. A DC motor drive example demonstrates near-oracle LQG performance without explicit noise covariance estimation.

papers.title: A Delay-Embedded Uncertainty-Aware Estimator for Trustworthy Cyber-Physical Systems
papers.abstract: Trustworthy cyber-physical systems require predictive models that can handle uncertainty when accurate physical models are unavailable and measurements are noisy. This work proposes an uncertainty-aware data-driven framework for one-step-ahead output prediction in nonlinear systems using delay-embedded input--output representations. A recurrent neural network learns a Gaussian second-order description of the future embedded state, while a Kalman-type correction step incorporates new measurements within a probabilistic filtering framework. The resulting estimator provides output predictive moments that are Fisher consistent, and calibrated uncertainty estimates that can support monitoring and anomaly detection in learning-enabled cyber-physical systems, without requiring Gaussianity of the true predictive distribution. Numerical results show performance comparable to a model-based extended Kalman filter without knowledge of the system dynamics.

papers.title: Continuous Hybrid Spatiotemporal Logic for Trustworthy CPS Specifications
papers.abstract: Trustworthy cyber-physical systems require specifications that capture where agents move, their clearance from critical regions, and whether mission objectives hold along continuous trajectories. This letter introduces continuous hybrid spatiotemporal logic (C-HSTL), a continuous-space language for spatially embedded CPSs in arbitrary finite-dimensional Euclidean workspaces. C-HSTL interprets propositions as time-varying regions, nominals as moving entities or stored viewpoints, and combines bounded temporal, metric-region, and hybrid-reference operators. We provide Boolean and compositional signed quantitative semantics, sign soundness, a nominal-trajectory perturbation certificate for the metric–hybrid fragment, and patterns for intrusion, clearance, reachability, separation, recovery, formation, and progress. The semantics distinguish exact nominal equality from tolerance-based certification and ordinary point-to-region distance from an outside-positive signed distance that preserves penetration depth. A two-dimensional drone case study demonstrates consistent finite-trace evaluation and time-localized diagnostic margins without spatial discretization.

papers.title: Real-Time Synthesis of Robust Controlled Invariant Sets for Monotone Systems
papers.abstract: Safety-critical control of autonomous systems requires formal safety certificates, such as controlled invariant sets, that must be computed online as conditions change. Although standard synthesis algorithms scale poorly with state dimension, monotone dynamical systems with lower-closed safety specifications allow for accelerated computation of controlled invariant sets. In particular, lazy fixed-point algorithms exploit monotonicity and track only the antichain basis of the set. However, membership tests and redundancy checks against an evolving basis remain major bottlenecks. We introduce a threshold-function reformulation in which a lower-closed set on a d-dimensional grid is represented by its column heights along a designated axis. This reformulates the greatest-fixed-point iteration as independent one-dimensional binary searches, one per grid column, yielding an embarrassingly parallel iteration with asymptotically lower computational complexity than the lazy fixed-point algorithm. Experiments synthesize invariant sets on 3D grids with 10^9 cells in under 50 ms and 10^14 cells in under two minutes. We further demonstrate online re-synthesis in a safety-informed model predictive controller example.

papers.title: Pole Assignment With Fixed Hidden Modes in Scalar Linear High-Order Differential Systems
papers.abstract: This letter studies pole assignment for scalar linear high-order differential systems with noncoprime plant polynomials. The auxiliary controller canonical realization generates the trajectories of the reduced equation rather than all trajectories of the unreduced equation, which also contains autonomous trajectories associated with the common factor. We distinguish these external trajectories from the internal unobservable dynamics of the realization. We then determine which feedback laws can be expressed through the state variable, the control input, and finitely many derivatives. Such laws leave the modes associated with the common factor fixed and give the corresponding restriction on assignable poles. For each expressible feedback, we characterize all differential equations within the prescribed bound on derivative order that represent the same feedback. Whether the control input disappears depends on the selected equation, whereas the number of independent input initial values is invariant among these equations. Finally, triangular closed-loop equations separate the dynamics associated with the common factor, the assignable dynamics, and the remaining input freedom, and yield exact initial-value descriptions. A two-mass vibration example illustrates the results.

papers.title: End-to-End Abstraction-Based Control with LLM-Enhanced NL-to-LTL Translation
papers.abstract: Abstraction-Based Controller Design (ABCD) offers a principled framework for the safe control of complex Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs), but interfacing real-world requirements with its formal synthesis machinery remains a major bottleneck: such requirements are most naturally expressed in Natural Language (NL), whereas ABCD requires formal specifications such as Linear Temporal Logic (LTL). Large Language Models (LLMs) offer a promising way to bridge this gap by translating NL requirements into formal specifications. This paper makes three contributions. First, we formalize an LLM-enhanced pipeline for ABCD, in which NL requirements are translated into LTL and used within a formal synthesis workflow. Second, we implement this pipeline in the Dionysos toolbox and introduce a benchmark for evaluating NL-to-LTL translation under both logical diversity and linguistic variation. Third, experiments with state-of-the-art LLMs reveal a consistent relationship between LTL complexity and translation success: translation accuracy decreases as the target specification becomes more complex in terms of Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) size, temporal depth, and Büchi automaton size, while accounting for NL input length. Together, these contributions provide both an evaluation framework and a practical integration pathway for making ABCD more accessible while preserving the rigor of formal methods.

papers.title: Structured Koopman–Kronecker Actor–Critic Learning for Nonlinear Optimal Control
papers.abstract: This letter proposes a structured actor–critic reinforcement learning framework for the optimal control of discrete-time nonlinear systems using Koopman-based lifted representations. In conventional actor–critic schemes, the actor and critic approximation spaces are typically selected independently, which can lead to poor approximation quality or require extensive trial-and-error in basis-function selection. To address this, we introduce a Koopman-Kronecker-structured critic whose features are constructed from the Kronecker product of the basis functions employed in the actor network. This construction is motivated by the quadratic structure that value functions admit in lifted coordinates, enabling a linear-in-the-parameters critic representation. Since the Kronecker product increases the critic dimension quadratically, a reduced-order variant utilizing singular value decomposition is developed to enhance computational efficiency. Numerical experiments on the Van der Pol and Duffing oscillators demonstrate that this structural coupling improves Bellman approximation and yields competitive closed-loop performance compared to independently designed actor–critic architectures.

papers.title: Formal Verification of Switched Systems via Path-Complete Closure Certificates
papers.abstract: We introducePath-Complete Closure Certificates(PC-CCs) for persistence verification of discrete-time nonlinear switched systems under arbitrary switching. PC-CCs assign relational certificates to ordered pairs of graph nodes, allowing edge-compatible composition of reachability evidence while retaining the graph endpoints of trajectory segments.We prove that path-completeness is necessary and sufficient for soundness of the resulting PC-CC rule over all switched systems. We also derive SOS sufficient conditions for polynomial data and a complementary rank-separated sufficient criterion that decouples graph-indexed reachability from scalar well-founded progress. The original PC-CC conditions are verified exactly on a scalable benchmark in dimensions 4, 8, and 16, whereas the separate reachability–rank criterion is verified by SOS on a nonlinear platoon exhibiting four transient visits. In a matched comparison, a two-node PC-CC family succeeds whereas every member of a specified one-node convex-projection family fails.

papers.title: Resilient Output Containment under Undisclosed Leader Dynamics and Actuator Attacks
papers.abstract: This work studies resilient output containment for heterogeneous linear multi-agent systems with actuator cyber-attacks over directed network topologies. The leaders generate bounded locally absolutely continuous trajectories; however, their dynamics, velocity bounds, and motion envelopes are undisclosed to the followers. The cyber-attack model includes state- and input-correlated, as well as bounded exogenous actuator false-data terms. A continuous two-layer adaptive control architecture is proposed. The first layer is a virtual-actuator reconfiguration layer that uses partial state measurements to compensate for actuator attacks in the local tracking-error dynamics. The second layer is a network interface that generates task-space commands via an adaptive interaction protocol. This protocol uses only neighbor-exchanged network-interface states whose dimensions match those of the plant output, and it does not require global graph knowledge for parameter tuning. For directed graphs, under a leader-rooted united spanning-tree condition, a nonsmooth Lyapunov analysis yields asymptotic containment at the command level. The physical outputs then converge to the leader convex hull up to a residual determined by the command-tracking local controllers. Simulation results using a network of quadrotors with damped suspended loads illustrate the performance of attack recovery and containment tracking.

papers.title: Trimmed fusion for resilient distributed Bayesian state estimation
papers.abstract: This letter addresses resilient fusion of probability density functions (PDFs) in distributed Bayesian state estimation.We propose a trimmed logarithmic opinion pooling (logOP) fusion rule which, given N available PDFs and an upper bound f < N/2 on the number of corrupted ones, selects the subset of cardinality N − f with minimum logOP fusion residual. Fusion is then performed by standard logOP over the selected subset. We show that the selected subset contains at least N − 2f reliable PDFs and that the resulting fused density satisfies a resilience bound, scaling as (N−f)/(N−2f), depending only on the dispersion of the reliable PDFs, not on the corrupted ones. A closed-form implementation for exponential-family PDFs and a distributed target-tracking example with cyber-attacked agents demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Output-feedback MPC under lossy actuation via dual constrained full-information estimation
papers.abstract: This paper addresses constrained output-feedback control of discrete-time linear systems subject to bounded disturbances and random packet losses in the controller-actuator channel. State estimation is performed using a constrained full-information estimator (CFIE) employing minimum-variance duality; we establish conditions for uniform boundedness of the resulting estimation error. We then compare the use of expectation-based nominal stochastic MPC without chance constraints (NSMPC) with an optimistic formulation that assumes no packets are dropped over the prediction horizon. We show that OMPC ensures a strictly positive lower bound on the one-step conditional probability of maintaining state-estimate feasibility, whereas NSMPC may admit subsets of the feasibility region from which feasibility is lost with probability one.

papers.title: Guaranteed Privacy of LQ Network Games via Payoff Perturbation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate privacy-preserving network games in which players protect sensitive payoff information during information aggregation. Unlike stochastic privacy mechanisms based on random noise injection, such as differential privacy (DP), we propose a deterministic guaranteed privacy (GP) framework using interval perturbations of payoff parameters. Specifically, we design a guaranteed privacy-preserving mechanism by characterizing the separation and overlap of perturbed equilibrium sets corresponding to adjacent payoff parameters. For linear–quadratic network games, necessary and sufficient conditions are derived to guarantee prescribed privacy levels, together with a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a feasible perturbation radius. Moreover, an explicit equilibrium error bound is established to characterize the privacy–accuracy tradeoff. Simulations validate the theoretical results and demonstrate that the proposed mechanism satisfies the prescribed privacy guarantees while yielding smaller deviations from the nominal Nash equilibrium than a stochastic DP benchmark under their respective privacy settings.

papers.title: Lyapunov-Level ${\mathcal{L}}_{{2}}$ -Attenuation Certificates Under Input Constraints
papers.abstract: This letter studies level-dependent${\mathcal {L}}_{2}$-attenuation certification for input-constrained nonlinear systems using a given nominal control Lyapunov function as a candidate storage function. A certificate feasibility map is derived that relates the prescribed attenuation bound, the Lyapunov sublevel set, and the minimum input bound needed for feasibility. The map establishes that tightening the attenuation requirement or enlarging the certified sublevel set yields a nondecreasing minimum input requirement. Conversely, under a fixed input limit, the attenuation bound certified by the inverse feasibility map is nondecreasing with the Lyapunov level. This feasibility structure motivates a Lyapunov-level dissipation allocation principle that strengthens dissipation on smaller levels while relaxing it on larger ones. Numerical examples illustrate the level-wise feasibility structure and the performance of the proposed Lyapunov-level dissipation allocation under input saturation.

papers.title: Control Laguerre Tessellation: Semi-Discrete Optimal Transport Over Control Systems
papers.abstract: We study the optimal transport of optimally controlled agents from a compactly supported absolutely continuous source to a discrete target measure. The ground cost for the transport is induced by the optimal cost of the agents' motion. When this ground cost satisfies the twist condition, the optimal transport map is given almost everywhere in terms of a Laguerre tessellation of the state space. We refer to this control-theoretic generalization of Laguerre tessellation as Control Laguerre Tessellation (CLT), and illustrate it for two ground costs induced by linear controlled agents with minimum energy and minimum time objectives.

papers.title: Reset-Based Distributed Optimization for Trustworthy Cyber-Physical Reconfiguration under Faults, Isolation and Recovery
papers.abstract: Networked cyber–physical systems (CPS) require distributed decision layers that can be reconfigured under failures, adversarial conditions, maintenance, or recovery. In distributed optimization, such membership changes modify the active objective and may leave edge information that biases gradient tracking. We propose Reset-DIGing, a distributed optimization algorithm combining a memory-based reformulation of Distributed Inexact Gradient tracking (DIGing) with local reset operations for cyber-physical reconfiguration under faults, isolation, and recovery. The resets restore the zero-sum exchange structure and gradient-tracking conservation identity, yielding convergence to the optimizer of the current active subnetwork under standard smoothness, strong-convexity, connectivity, and stepsize conditions. Its layered formulation supports different CPS reconfiguration policies, including monitoring, safety, trust, recovery, connectivity, and higher-level coordination. Simulations show network/control reconfiguration after failure, forced isolation, and recovery.

papers.title: Uniform Polynomial Stability of a Midpoint-Staggered Finite-Difference Scheme for a Wave Equation With Dynamic Boundary Control
papers.abstract: A structure-preserving midpoint-staggered finite-difference scheme is analyzed for a one-dimensional wave equation coupled to a first-order dynamic boundary controller. The continuous system has the polynomial energy-decay rate${t}^{\text {-1}}$, and the main question is whether this rate is preserved uniformly under spatial semi-discretization despite high-frequency numerical effects. The scheme combines nodal variables with midpoint averages and edge differences and preserves the exact discrete dissipation identity. Its staggered structure also yields an exact frequency-domain edge-energy propagation law, avoiding a discretization-dependent high-frequency remainder. We establish a quadratic high-frequency resolvent bound uniformly with respect to the discretization parameter and consequently obtain uniform${t}^{\text {-1}}$energy decay for the semi-discrete family. Numerical spectra are consistent with the corresponding inverse-square high-frequency behavior as the discretization is refined. No spectral filtering or artificial viscosity is required.

papers.title: Topology Reconfiguration of Multiagent Systems under Link Failures
papers.abstract: This work addresses fault-tolerant cooperative control in homogeneous multiagent systems subject to abrupt and potentially permanent communication link failures. A double-gain control law that decouples stabilization from consensus reduces consensus to the simultaneous stabilization of the disagreement dynamics, solved via a linear matrix inequality that gives a single pair of gains valid across every predefined safe topology and driving isolated agents to the origin. The global closed-loop dynamics are then modeled as a hybrid system that explicitly represents link failures and topology reconfigurations as discrete jump events updating a time-varying Laplacian. A distributed reconfiguration protocol restores consensus after each failure by switching to an admissible safe topology selected through a cost function balancing topology deviation and convergence rate. A common Lyapunov function establishes exponential consensus with an explicit convergence rate, provided a dwell-time condition relating the duration of the degraded phase to that of the safe phase holds; stabilizability of the agent dynamics is the only condition required by the gain design. Disconnected topologies yield cluster consensus during the degraded phase, and the protocol returns the agents to the origin when no safe topology remains admissible. The approach is illustrated through a formation-control case study on a vehicle platoon.

papers.title: Collusion Detection in Multi-Agent Games
papers.abstract: Collusion arises when a subset of agents coordinate covertly through privately sharing information. By inducing dependence among their actions that cannot be explained by publicly observed signals under independent play, colluding agents can achieve higher payoffs in a manner that violates fairness or regulatory constraints. We study the problem of detecting collusion by a passive external observer in multi-agent games from repeated observations of the joint actions of the agents, when the observer has no access to the payoffs, strategies, or covert communications among the agents. We show that, under a finite-sample graph-recoverability condition, detecting such collusion reduces to testing conditional independence (CI) relations among the actions of the agents conditioned on publicly observable variables. By leveraging existing finite-sample guarantees for CI testing over finite discrete distributions [1], we derive non-asymptotic sample complexity bounds for detecting collusion with high probability. These tests can be composed via PC-type structure-learning algorithms to recover the dependency graph over agents’ actions with the connected components of this graph corresponding to the colluding coalitions. Our results characterize how the required number of rounds scales with the detectability threshold, the number of agents, and the sizes of the conditioning sets.

papers.title: Delay-Induced Acceleration of Network Consensus
papers.abstract: We study the speed of consensus in first-order networks with time delays. Although transmission delays typically slow convergence, we show that they can accelerate consensus in certain special network topologies. We define acceleration using the spectral abscissa of all characteristic roots except the simple root at zero and derive exact expressions for these roots in terms of the Lambert-$W$function. Spectral inequalities involving the real and imaginary parts of the nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues give sufficient conditions for local acceleration under transmission and processing delays. The characteristic-root formulas also yield computable acceleration intervals, including the effect of the transmission dynamics along the agreement subspace, and processing-delay stability limits. We show that, among connected undirected unweighted graphs, only complete graphs exhibit acceleration under sufficiently small transmission delays. We present examples of noncomplete directed graphs that exhibit delay-induced acceleration.

papers.title: Adaptive Neural Network Control of Fractional-Order Nonlinear Systems via Integer-Order Learning: A Memory-Efficient Approach
papers.abstract: This letter develops an integer-order (IO) neural-learning approach for a class of fractional-order (FO) nonlinear systems. An initialization-compensated (IC) filtered tracking error yields an exact IO control-relevant error dynamics, while retaining the FO plant dynamics. This enables IO neural-weight adaptation without fractional convolution in the NN learning channels. A neural network (NN) approximates the unknown nonlinearity on a prescribed compact state domain, while a robust discontinuous term compensates for the bounded ideal approximation residual. A nonsmooth Lyapunov analysis establishes semi-global asymptotic tracking. Besides, a reconstruction lemma provides the link between the IC filtered error convergence and the FO tracking errors. The proposed learning mechanism reduces the NN adaptive-law update time by about 99.67%, while preserving tracking performance comparable to a conventional FO adaptive NN controller, with RMSE values of approximately 0.033.

papers.title: Privacy-Induced Alignment in Finite-Rate Strategic Estimation
papers.abstract: We study privacy as an alignment mechanism in a static strategic finite-rate estimation game. An encoder observes a state variableXand private bias Θ, sends a public finite-rate message, and anticipates two minimum mean-square error (MMSE) followers: a legitimate estimator ofXand an eavesdropper estimating Θ. The encoder wants the legitimate estimate close toX+ Θ. We derive a distribution-free influence bound and a receiver performance guarantee under a common privacy constraint. For jointly Gaussian variables, we solve the deterministic and randomized one-bit problem globally: the optimal strategic quantizer is a balanced halfspace determined by a generalized eigenvector. We characterize all attainable binary posterior covariances and use convex duality to prove that the one-bit Gaussian hard-privacy problem has no scalarization gap. For independent standard Gaussians, we give closed-form scalarized one-bit distortions. For arbitrary rates and sources with an independent-residual decomposition, we characterize maximal privacy. The analysis also shows that a privacy incentive or constraint can improve legitimate estimation by limiting the sender’s strategic influence. Under correlation, however, the loss of useful state information can outweigh this benefit.

papers.title: Normalized Negative Imaginary Synthesis for a Class of Nonlinear Descriptor Systems
papers.abstract: This paper studies normalized nonlinear negative imaginary (NI) synthesis for nonlinear descriptor systems with Lipschitz-type perturbations. A proportional derivative output feedback (PDOF) controller is employed such that the resulting closed-loop system is a normal nonlinear NI system with degree α. By using an augmented descriptor representation, sufficient linear matrix inequality (LMI) conditions are derived for PDOF synthesis, and an optimization formulation is given to maximize the perturbation bound. The framework is further extended by introducing a stable dynamic evaluation path and certifying the resulting augmented port. Two examples are presented to verify the proposed design method.

papers.title: Safe Navigation Using a Geometric Controller and Control Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: Mobile robot navigation in obstacle-rich environments requires smooth target tracking together with reliable safety assurance. Inspired by the geometric error representation of geometric model predictive control (GMPC), this letter combines a lightweight body-frame geometric nominal controller with control barrier functions (CBFs). The controller generates a goal-directed nominal input without finite-horizon optimization, while a CBF-based quadratic program enforces obstacle avoidance. Furthermore, a short-duration tangential correction mechanism is introduced to alleviate conservative behavior and stagnation near constrained goal regions. Simulation results show that the proposed framework achieves smooth motion, safe obstacle avoidance, and improved goal-reaching performance in constrained environments.

papers.title: Continuous Gradients for Learning and Optimization in Feedback Control
papers.abstract: This letter develops a regret-based analysis of continuous-time optimization in closed-loop control systems, connecting online learning objectives with control-theoretic requirements. Two constrained update mechanisms are studied: a projected dynamical system (PDS), which projects the instantaneous descent velocity onto the tangent cone of the feasible set, and a projected gradient flow (PGF), which relaxes a finite projected-gradient step into continuous time. For convex online losses, the analysis establishes distinct regret upper bounds and clarifies the limiting relation between these mechanisms. The framework is applied to closed-loop residual model learning, and numerical examples illustrate key properties of both approaches.

papers.title: Foundations of Machine-Checked Control Theory in Lean
papers.abstract: We introduce an open-source library for machine-checked control theory in the interactive proof assistant Lean to lay foundations for the verification of cyber-physical systems. To this end, as representative theorems, we present formalizations of Lyapunov stability theory and the small-gain theorem. First, the machinery employed for formalizing Lyapunov stability, i.e., neighborhood filters, allows stating a Lyapunov theorem that covers both points and sets and applies to continuous, discrete, and hybrid systems. Second, the small-gain theorem is proved via stating input-output systems as relations without the usual well-posedness assumption. The Lean formalization of each of these theorems is then presented. We conclude by discussing the library architecture and mentioning some of the other system theoretic results that are formalized in the library along with future plans.

papers.title: Data-Driven Design of Deadbeat Observers for Higher-Order LTI Systems
papers.abstract: In this letter, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of a deadbeat observer (DBO) for systems described by higher-order difference equations based on finite historical data. Furthermore, we develop an algorithm to construct a consistent DBO and to parametrise all DBOs directly from the historical data. Finally, we apply the proposed approach to the problem of state estimation in the presence of unknown inputs.

papers.title: Knowledge-guided attack detection and diagnosis for trustworthy cyber-physical systems
papers.abstract: Attack detection in Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) is hindered by adversaries capable of preserving the local plausibility of measurements while exploiting dependencies among coupled subsystems. This study proposes the Knowledge-guided Heterogeneous Graph Network (KHGN), a neuro-symbolic architecture that represents the CPS as a typed heterogeneous graph, integrating three complementary dimensions: temporal sensor dynamics, physical topology of the system, and domain knowledge formalized through an ontology. The effectiveness of the approach is evaluated on the Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) industrial testbed for multi-stage attack detection. Across five independent runs, KHGN achieved a macro F1 of 0.928 ± 0.006 and exceeded the HGT-only variant by 14.3 percentage points. Limited-label and leave-one-attack-out evaluations further assessed performance under scarce supervision and for attacks excluded from training.

papers.title: Online Learning of Neural State-Space Models
papers.abstract: Recent advances in deep-learning-based nonlinear system identification have led to encoder-based estimation of neural state-space (ANN-SS) models that achieve state-of-the-art performance in offline settings by estimating initial model states from past input-output data. These methods are typically used in multiple-shooting-based offline identification, and online learning of these models remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a batch-wise learning pipeline and a direct recursive identification algorithm for subspace encoder-based ANN-SS models. We provide convergence analysis of the recursive formulation and validate its performance through extensive simulation studies. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach enables computationally efficient online adaptation with high model accuracy.

papers.title: Event-Driven Self-Organized Fencing Control for Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems With an Unknown Time-Varying Target
papers.abstract: This letter investigates the event-triggered self-organized fencing control problem for second-order multi-agent systems subject to external disturbances and an unknown time-varying target. Unlike prescribed fencing configurations, a self-organized formation is generated through potential-field regulation rather than prescribed relative positions. Based on the velocity compensation function, a regulation potential function is constructed to drive the agents towards the target while the collision and obstacle avoidance potentials are further incorporated to guarantee the local safety. A dynamic controller is then developed where a smooth reinforcement learning echo state network (RL-ESN) compensation function is introduced to attenuate bounded disturbances. Furthermore, an event-driven mechanism with a safety-regulation function is designed to guarantee the system safety and reduce the unnecessary data transmission between the controller and actuators. The rigorous theoretical analysis illustrates that the regulation and tracking error signals are uniformly ultimately bounded. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: Control Synthesis for Security Hyperproperties via Control Barrier Functions
papers.abstract: Many security and privacy requirements in cyber-physical systems are inherently relational, involving comparisons across multiple system trajectories, rather than properties of single trajectories. These requirements, known as hyperproperties, naturally arise in information-flow security, and include opacity, noninterference, and K-anonymity. Since standard temporal logics are limited to single-trajectory specifications, HyperLTL has emerged as a powerful tool for specifying such relational requirements. This paper presents a control synthesis framework for enforcing a class of HyperLTL security specifications in continuous-time control-affine systems using control barrier functions (CBFs). The proposed approach constructs CBFs over an augmented state space that captures the multiple trajectories quantified in the HyperLTL formula. The resulting barrier conditions are imposed as constraints in a quadratic program, enabling real-time controller synthesis that enforces hyperproperties. The framework provides a unified approach for integrating information-flow security requirements into continuous-time controller synthesis.We show how representative security notions can be encoded and enforced within this framework, and demonstrate its effectiveness through a robotic case study.
