papers.title: Conformal Constraint Tightening for Chance-Constrained Motion Planning With Unknown Dynamics
papers.abstract: Motion planning algorithms compute control sequences that drive autonomous robots to goal regions while avoiding unsafe states. Existing methods, from sampling-based planning to deep reinforcement learning, typically provide task-completion guarantees only with respect to a nominal model or simulator, which may be invalidated when the true dynamics are unknown or difficult to model accurately. This letter addresses this limitation for systems with unknown dynamics and an available approximate nominal model, contributing a planner-agnostic constraint-tightening procedure that equips existing planners with a probabilistic task-completion guarantee on the true system. We leverage conformal prediction to provide a probabilistic bound on the nominal-to-true trajectory deviation over a distribution of planning problems. We tighten the planning constraints using that bound, and show that solving the tightened problem under the nominal model is a sufficient condition for solving the original problem on the true system with a prescribed probability. We validate the theoretical guarantees empirically and demonstrate substantially improved task completion relative to nominal-model planning.

papers.title: Adaptive Saturated ADRC of a Piezoelectric Drug-Delivery Actuator With Cubic Damping and Dahl Hysteresis
papers.abstract: This letter develops an adaptive saturated ADRC scheme for position tracking of a piezoelectric actuator (PEA) for liquid drug delivery. The actuator combines cubic viscous damping with Dahl hysteresis, its effective input gain is unknown, and the driving voltage saturates. An extended-state observer, driven by the applied voltage, reconstructs the unmeasured velocity and the matched plant perturbation from position measurements alone, while a projection-based adaptive law keeps the nominal input gain inside a known positive interval. In contrast with cancellation-based designs, the cubic damping is retained in the closed loop: its dissipativity confines the trajectories, so the operating envelope is derived, and it absorbs the damping mismatch in the observer, so no lower bound on the observer bandwidth is required. The tracking and observer errors are proven semiglobally uniformly ultimately bounded, and simulations confirm the analysis under active saturation.

papers.title: Learning-Enabled Parameter Synthesis for Nonlinear Systems From Signal Temporal Logic
papers.abstract: Signal Temporal Logic (STL) is increasingly used to describe interpretable objectives and constraints for optimal control and learning methods, especially when no target time series data is available. In this work, we propose to synthesize parameters for nonlinear systems that robustly satisfy continuous-time STL specifications for uncertain initial conditions. To this end, we use gradient-based optimization along with set-based reachability verification to efficiently learn in high-dimensional parameter spaces while providing provable satisfaction guarantees for the optimized parameters. We demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of our method on three systems with up to 18 parameter dimensions.

papers.title: Robust Stabilization of Constrained Linear Time-Delay Systems via Output Feedback
papers.abstract: We address the problem of robust stabilization for constrained discrete-time linear systems with state delay. We develop a set-theoretic static output-feedback framework that formally guarantees constraint satisfaction and robust stability despite the presence of bounded disturbances and delays. In the proposed framework, we first compute a robust controlD-invariant set together with an associated static output-feedback gain. The set of states that can be made to converge to the computed invariant set with the help of feasible control actions is then computed along with feasible static output-feedback gains by solving a sequence of bilinear optimization problems. We employ zonotopes as set representations to describe the invariant and controllable sets. We then propose a switching control law which ensures constraint satisfaction and contraction towards theD-invariant set for all states present inside the approximated set of robust stabilizable states. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach using numerical simulations.

papers.title: Controller-Agnostic Runtime Safety Certificates for Tool-Using AI Agents via Data-Driven Robust Reachability
papers.abstract: Software agents built on large language models act by issuing tool calls, some of which cannot be undone. To control theory the model is an opaque feedback controller, replaced every few months, whose closed loop cannot be analyzed directly. We propose a runtime filter, or shield, between any such controller and its environment that certifies a bound on the probability of reaching an unsafe condition during a bounded task. Given a predicate abstraction and candidate successor sets, everything else comes from logs. The loop becomes a finite controlled Markov chain, the estimated kernel is surrounded by a distribution-free confidence set, and robust reach–avoid value iteration runs over it. The certificate is probably approximately correct and uniform over controllers respecting the filter, so one model may replace another without recomputation. In all tested datasets the true risk stays within certificate and budget; in a file-system sandbox the filter stays sound against a hazard absent from the logs, where a plug-in baseline certifies safety and fails; and it holds seven controllers, six built on open-weights models, to zero unsafe outcomes in 1,050 episodes.

papers.title: Protection against Colluding Eavesdroppers in Distributed Dynamical Systems
papers.abstract: In this letter, we study terminal-state protection in distributed dynamical systems under colluding eavesdroppers. Many distributed protocols, including consensus, distributed optimization, and federated learning, drive agents to a common terminal decision x⋆. External adversaries may attempt to reconstruct this terminal state by eavesdropping on the messages exchanged among the honest agents. While prior work characterizes protection against a single eavesdropper, we consider multiple adversaries that collude by sharing local reconstructions through an adversarial aggregation mechanism. We derive an exact characterization of the terminal mean-square protection achieved against the colluded estimate. The result yields a bias-variance decomposition in which weights are determined by the adversarial consensus gains, revealing how collusion reduces protection through bias cancellation and residual-variance averaging. We further characterize when collusion improves upon individual no-collusion estimates and how protection depends on the number of adversaries and gain heterogeneity. Numerical experiments on distributed logistic regression validate the theory and illustrate the role of the adversarial gain profile.

papers.title: An Efficient Parallel Solver for Linear-Equality-Constrained LQR Problems
papers.abstract: We present a parallel solver for finite-horizon linear-quadratic regulator (LQR) problems with arbitrary stagewise linear equality constraints, using linear work and logarithmic depth in the horizon for fixed local dimensions. The solver uses a two-part reduction that separates feasibility from optimization. First, an associative suffix scan computes the states from which each remaining horizon is feasible. Second, we use these feasible-continuation sets to eliminate the constraints independently at each stage, producing an unconstrained LQR problem with smaller or equal, possibly stage-varying dimensions. A parallel unconstrained-LQR solver completes the primal solution. Finally, we recover valid multipliers from the original KKT stationarity equations using a logarithmic-depth contraction-expansion procedure, even when the multipliers are not unique. Sequential and parallel implementations are validated against dense KKT solutions and original residuals. We release a C++/CUDA implementation with JAX bindings under the MIT license.

papers.title: Attack Detection using Time Series Foundation Models
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of attack detection in cyber-physical systems, where the detector operates without any knowledge of the plant model or its structure. A remotely located plant transmits sensor measurements to an operator over a network that is under attack. We propose a model-structure-free detector based onTimesFM, a time-series foundation model developed by Google Research, which serves as a surrogate residual generator operating in a zero-shot fashion, and characterize its detection power at attack onset. To evaluate the detector against worst-case attacks, we consider model-free replay attacks and, assuming an attacker with full model knowledge, derive closed-form optimal stealthy attacks against a χ2detector, exact for linear and first-order approximate for nonlinear systems. We show empirically, on a mass-spring system and the IEEE 14-bus power system, that attacks stealthy against the model-based detector are detected by theTimesFM-based detector, which performs comparably to or better than a trained Long Short-Term Memory baseline, without any training. We also empirically show thatTimesFMpredictions can substitute corrupted measurements when classical redundancy assumptions fail.

papers.title: Distribution-Free Budgeted Stealthy Attack Scheduling for Remote State Estimation
papers.abstract: This letter addresses budgeted stealthy false-data-injection (FDI) scheduling against remote state estimation, where a resource-constrained adversary may corrupt at most a fraction Γ of transmissions. Existing event-triggered schedulers invert a Gaussian innovation tail to set the firing threshold and certify stealth by covariance matching; both are exact only under Gaussianity, which real cyber-physical residuals routinely violate. We propose a distribution-free scheduler pairing the worst-case FDI action with a split-conformal calibrated trigger, requiring neither the plant matrices nor any distributional model. We establish exact pathwise stealth against every magnitude-measurable detector, for any firing rule and innovation law; a finite-sample distribution-free bound on the mean firing rate, with almost-sure budget attainment under stationarity and ergodicity; and a steady-state degradation identity linear in a single scalar energy capture Ψ, maximized by the same order statistic that delivers the budget guarantee. A conditional sign-symmetry condition delimits when the certificate extends to sign-sensitive detectors, the residual exposure being governed by a fourth cumulant that vanishes under Gaussian noise. Monte-Carlo studies and a heavy-duty-truck CAN record confirm the bounds and quantify what the Gaussian assumption costs outside its regime.

papers.title: Sequential Trajectory Planning for Semi-Rigid Ackermann Formations with Fixed Separating Hyperplanes
papers.abstract: This letter presents a sequential method for planning trajectories of semi-rigid formations of Ackermann-steered vehicles in cluttered environments. A curvature-based representation and the nonholonomic no-slip condition express the follower paths algebraically in terms of the leader path, preserving offsets in the leader frame while allowing different vehicle orientations. Collision avoidance uses shared separating hyperplanes that account for the rectangular footprints of all formation members. A samplingbased search supplies an initial path, from which the Separating Axis Theorem constructs the hyperplanes. The path is optimized with these planes held fixed within each solve; very short forward or reverse sections are removed from the initialization before geometric re-optimization. Speed-profile optimization on the fixed path then balances travel duration against control variation under every vehicle’s speed, acceleration and steering-rate limits. Adaptive numerical checks assess clearance and physical constraints between nodes. Simulations in two cluttered environments demonstrate the approach.

papers.title: Event-Triggered State Agreement of PWM-Controlled Multi-Agent Systems With Jointly Connected Switching Networks
papers.abstract: This paper studies the state agreement problem for continuous-time multi-agent systems actuated by pulse-width-modulated (PWM) controllers whose sampling periods are generated by event-triggered mechanisms. In contrast with fixed-period PWM consensus, the sign and duty ratio of each PWM input are computed from a locally stored disagreement variable that is refreshed only when a state-dependent triggering condition is violated. This setting captures digital implementations in which computation and actuation are intentionally slowed down when the local disagreement is small, while high update rates are recovered when the disagreement is large. With the proposed event-trigger-based control protocol, the achievement of asymptotic state agreement is guaranteed and Zeno behavior is excluded provided that a uniformly quasi-strong connectivity condition is satisfied. The result reduces to the classical periodic-sampling PWM consensus when all sampling periods are constant. In addition, the result is extended to the self-triggered sampling case. Numerical examples demonstrate that the event-triggered PWM controller achieves state agreement with substantially fewer duty-ratio updates than a fixed-period implementation.

papers.title: Beyond Ellipsoids: Semialgebraic Tightening for Chance Constraints Under Actuator Saturation
papers.abstract: Motivated by stochastic model predictive control applications, we develop a semialgebraic framework for constraint tightening in chance-constrained systems with unbounded additive disturbances and saturated inputs. The saturation nonlinearity is represented exactly through its semialgebraic description. A polynomial Lyapunov function satisfying a stochastic drift condition is then synthesized using sum-of-squares optimization, yielding finite-time probabilistic reachable sets and probabilistic ultimate bound. The resulting sets are further optimized through an objective tailored to constraint tightening. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness and scalability properties of the approach.

papers.title: On the Exact Discretization of Exponential Predefined-Time Controllers
papers.abstract: Digital realization is challenging for exponential predefined-time controllers, whose gain vanishes at the origin yet grows faster than every power of the state. For the scalar closed loop, this letter delineates the failure of forward Euler by the two real branches of the Lambert W function and analyzes the exact discretization generated by the settling-time function, which reproduces the closed loop of the sampled integrator at the sampling instants and settles in a number of steps bounded uniformly in the initial condition. Its feedback never exceeds that of the semi-implicit benchmark at the same state, and along trajectories it uses the same total input with no larger peak and no more control energy, whereas the semi-implicit scheme settles at least as fast. Under bounded matched disturbances, its exact ultimate bound exceeds the continuous-time residual by less than the disturbance accumulated over one sampling period, whereas that of the semi-implicit scheme is no larger. A spacecraft example illustrates the results.

papers.title: Model Predictive Path Integral Control as a Quantum Query Problem
papers.abstract: Model predictive path integral (MPPI) control computes its inputs as cost-weighted averages over simulated trajectories. However, it typically requires many simulations, especially when low-cost trajectories are rare. We therefore formulate this computation as a quantum query problem. By replacing Gaussian input perturbations with random signs, we express the MPPI update as a ratio of averages over a finite set of perturbation sequences. We then construct quantum circuits that encode these averages as measurement probabilities, which allows quantum amplitude estimation to compute the update with fewer queries than classical sampling. Numerical examples confirm the predicted query scalings and show that a quantum advantage requires many perturbation sequences.

papers.title: Interval-Observer Based Event-Triggered Consensus of Multi-Agent Systems with Disturbances
papers.abstract: This paper investigates event-triggered consensus of multi-agent systems subject to bounded disturbances. An interval-observer-based framework is developed to provide guaranteed state enclosures, where the midpoint estimation error is incorporated into the consensus analysis. The input-to-state stability of the midpoint estimation error and the uniform ultimate boundedness of disagreement dynamics are established, together with a positive lower bound of inter-event times. Simulation results verify the robustness and communication efficiency of the proposed method.

papers.title: Distributed Simultaneous Estimation of the State, Unknown Input, and Output Disturbance in Discrete-Time Linear Systems
papers.abstract: This paper studies the distributed observer design problem for discrete-time linear systems subject to bounded unknown inputs and local output disturbances. The system is monitored by a network of sensor nodes connected through a directed communication graph, with each node having access only to a portion of the system output. To address this setting, we propose a distributed observer that enables each node to estimate the global state, the unknown input, and its own local output disturbance simultaneously. We show that the estimation error at each node is ℓ∞-stable with a quantifiable performance level. Explicit upper bounds are derived for the unknown input reconstruction error and the local output disturbance reconstruction error. The observer gain matrices are obtained by solving a set of linear matrix inequalities (LMIs). Numerical simulations are conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method and validate the theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Dynamic Nash equilibria in logical dynamic games with impulse control
papers.abstract: This article studies deterministic finite-horizon two-player logical dynamic games with impulse control, in which Player 1 acts on the stepping dynamics and Player 2 applies impulse controls when the state enters the impulsive set. First, necessary and sufficient conditions are established for forward completeness of the impulsive logical system, characterizing whether the jumping process can be terminated after finitely many impulses. Second, a state-strategy coevolutionary framework is proposed, in which the strategy updating dynamics and the logical state dynamics are integrated to characterize their joint evolution. Under this framework, the finite-horizon dynamic game is decomposed, via dynamic programming, into a sequence of static time-sliced games. Based on this decomposition, verifiable algebraic criteria are derived under which the generated strategy trajectories form dynamic Nash equilibrium strategies over the planning horizon. An illustrative example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the theoretical results.

papers.title: Mode-Weighted Transport Certificates for State-Dependent Reflected Switching Diffusions
papers.abstract: State-dependent switching diffusions can contract in law even when individual modes are expansive. We establish a computable, constant-one contraction certificate on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and compact convex domains with normal reflection. The mode-weighted transport cost combines spatial separation with a discrete graph penalty and retains spatial dependence when the modes differ. A synchronous Brownian coupling and a maximal coupling of jump clocks in equal modes lead to separate equal- and unequal-mode generator inequalities. We give a complete regularization argument for the nonsmooth cost, including the drift and jump errors, the sign of reflection, and the limiting Itô-Dynkin calculation. A resolvent proof transfers contraction to probability-valued weak solutions of the no-flux Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov system, while an explicit Foster-Lyapunov condition ensures existence and uniqueness of an invariant law on the whole space. For fixed weight ordering and decay rate, certificate synthesis is a semi-infinite linear feasibility problem; on compact domains, a Lipschitz-buffered finite mesh provides a rigorous test. One-dimensional and planar examples illustrate the certificate and its numerical verification.

papers.title: State Augmentation for Discrete-Time Lipschitz Observer Design: A Gain-Independent Obstruction and ρ-Contractive Synthesis
papers.abstract: A scalar-multiplier LMI widely used for discrete-time Lipschitz observers requires a sub-unit Lipschitz constant. This letter identifies the corresponding obstruction for the factored LMI family: feasibility imposes a necessary inequality linking the prescribed decay rate to the first nonzero coupling between the nonlinear increment and its argument. For a state lift by the nonlinearity this condition is gain independent and forces the Lipschitz constant of the one-step composite map below the squared rate. The lift therefore transfers the obstruction to a different map, and a sub-unit composite constant alone does not ensure feasibility. We give the implementable observer, a reduced lift, a diagonal-multiplier extension, and an ℓ2-gain synthesis accounting for disturbances inside the lifted nonlinearity. Explicit certificates and reproducible nominal, noisy and mismatch simulations compare the lift with native factorization, differential-mean-value/LPV certification and direct output injection, showing both how the lift can certify a super-unit original constant and why existing structure can be preferable to augmentation.
